title: Womack Sisters: the soul dynasty reborn
subtitle: Daughters of a musical tradition, they return to the family path after hard times
excerpt: In London, the Womack Sisters show that soul still reverberates, despite criticism and a past of Ubers and doubts.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Behind the scenes of a festival in London on a Sunday afternoon, the Womack Sisters settle onto a sofa still wearing the outfits they performed in moments earlier. The black dresses, tights and high heels create an elegant look, but ill-suited to the intense heat that dominates the venue.

A legacy that spans generations

The names surrounding the trio are well known in the soul world: their parents, both bearing the Womack surname, Uncle Bobby who achieved superstar status, and, further back, grandfather Sam Cooke, also remembered as an icon of the genre. This family heritage creates a direct link to one of the greatest dynasties in soul music.

From the wheel to the microphone

Before returning to the artistic path, the three went through a period driving ride-hailing vehicles, while listeners kept telling them that soul had lost its relevance. This mix of economic need and external disbelief spurred a decision: to go back to the family business and perpetuate the musical tradition passed down to them.

With the comeback, the Womack Sisters reaffirm the continuity of a legacy that, according to them, comes from the heart. Returning to the stage is not just a professional choice, but a reaffirmation of a musical identity that spans generations, showing that, even in the face of external doubts, the passion for soul remains alive.

With information from The Guardian.
